question: Your calm redline asked for 8 out of 10 from the agent judge on clean and aligned. After four passes the boxed marks are tidy, but the score is stuck near 5 to 6 and hand-drawn ideals of this screen score about 6 too. Close it on the pictures, go back to the older layout the judge likes better, or keep going for 8?
context: Three passes on 2026-11-11 moved the readouts to pt, added end ticks, then tidied placement. Scores (Ask, out of 100): older layout 72 to 75, current 63 to 65; clean about 5 now. Hand-placed ideals of this screen judged 5.0 to 6.3 on clean. Pictures: the redline's own drawing of the settings screenshot, before on the left, now on the right, boxes on what changed.

options.label: Close it on the pictures (right)
options.summary: The redline stays as on the right: numbers say pt, brackets hug what they measure, the field width runs inside the field, no mark touches another, no long lines to a number. The task closes for good.
pros: Meets every point of your read: no leg running into another mark, no long leader, brackets on their objects
Frees the loop for the next feature after four passes in one day
cons: The agent judge scores it about 10 points lower than the older layout
The judge calls hugging brackets a little crowded
options.mitigation: If a redline looks wrong to you later, say so on the picture and it comes back as a new task with that example.

options.label: Go back to the left layout
options.summary: Numbers ride brackets set a little off their objects, as on the left, keeping pt and end ticks. The 220 pt bracket stands above the field and its leg runs toward the 26 pt mark; 12 pt hangs lower on a longer line. Then the task closes.
pros: The agent judge scores it highest (72 to 75)
Every number sits on its own bracket
cons: Brings back the leg-into-another-mark and the long line to 12 pt you called clumsy
options.mitigation: One more short pass that restores the older placement and keeps the pt and end-tick work.

options.label: Keep going for 8
options.summary: More passes at the layout until the judge scores 8 on clean and aligned for this screen, judged first on the score.
pros: Holds to the bar you set
cons: Hand-drawn redlines of this same screen score about 6 from the same judge, so 8 may not exist here
Each pass takes the loop for hours ahead of other work
options.mitigation: Cap it at two more passes and come back with the best of them.
